title: JALLIANWALA BAGH
subtitle: The Garden the Empire Could Not Bury
intro: A film about 13 April 1919, built from a notice, a wall, a watch, a well and a report. No stock footage. No bodies. No paid APIs. Every frame is assembled on free GitHub Actions hardware.

stats.label: sourced lines
stats.note: every line carries a source id

firstCut.label: First cut
firstCut.note: Two static plates per scene, long holds and sparse lower-thirds. It read as a narrated slideshow, not a film.

currentCut.label: Investigative cut
currentCut.note: A 3.7-second average shot, a cold open, full-screen figures, evidence inserts, a layered score and burned-in captions.

transitionFamilies.name: Whip
transitionFamilies.use: Across connected spaces: notice to wall, watch to wall, wall to gate.

transitionFamilies.name: Match
transitionFamilies.use: Same object, new scale: the notice, the report, the well, the watch.

transitionFamilies.name: Flash
transitionFamilies.use: Date, order and casualty cards. Used as punctuation, never as decoration.

transitionFamilies.name: Dip
transitionFamilies.use: The silence before the firing and the gaps between argument.

transitionFamilies.name: Mask
transitionFamilies.use: The wall and the report revealed as evidence, edge first.

transitionFamilies.name: Crossfade
transitionFamilies.use: Only where two images belong to the same thought.

transitionFamilies.name: Hard cut
transitionFamilies.use: The cold open and the title. No softening.

pipeline.title: Source lock
pipeline.body: The storyboard is a JSON contract. Every narration line names a source. The validator refuses unsourced lines, missing shots and filler before a runner is allowed to render.

pipeline.title: Procedural sets
pipeline.body: Blender 4.2 builds the notice, wall, gate, watch, well, report, lamp and memorial as still plates. No stock images. No generated faces.

pipeline.title: Narration
pipeline.body: Piper reads the script locally with en_US-lessac-medium. No cloud narration, no per-word billing, no API key in the repository.

pipeline.title: Camera and type
pipeline.body: Chromium drives the timeline frame by frame: push-ins, pans, match cuts, mask wipes, impact cards and captions. The camera is code, so every frame is repeatable.

pipeline.title: Score and master
pipeline.body: ffmpeg synthesises the drone, clock, heartbeat and sub impacts, mixes the narration, burns the SRT into the master and encodes the MP4.

pipeline.title: Free CI
pipeline.body: The render runs on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu CPU. No GPU. No paid runner. The owner's machine writes the code; it does not render the film.

iterations.title: The first cut was rejected
iterations.body: 13 shots, 152 seconds, static plates and no burned captions. The note was blunt: it feels like a regular video. It was not shipped as the final film.

iterations.title: The sets were fixed before the edit
iterations.body: The wall, gate, well and notice were rebuilt. Bad compositions were removed. The empty threshold became a plate of its own so the aftermath could be shown without reconstructing the killing.

iterations.title: The cut became an investigation
iterations.body: The storyboard moved to 50 shots across nine scenes: the order, the garden, the exits, the ten minutes, the count, the well, the inquiry and the argument. Figures became full-frame cards. Transitions became part of the argument.

iterations.title: The 1080 master is gated
iterations.body: The previous 1080 render was cancelled because it used the rejected edit. A new master is only published after the investigative cut passes review.

rules: No bodies, no blood, no reconstructed killing. The wall, the well and the record carry the violence.
No number on screen without a source or an explicit attribution.
No stock footage and no generated faces. Every set is procedural.
No paid API keys. The pipeline must run on free CI.
If the edit is weak, the render does not ship.
